title: FeatureScript Compile Safety
summary: Use conservative FeatureScript APIs and parameter preconditions so generated code is more likely to compile on the first paste.
parameterHints: Expose dimensions with annotation defaults plus isLength(definition.name, LENGTH_BOUNDS).
Use isInteger for counts such as teeth, holes, and pattern instances.
modelingNotes: Call skSolve before opExtrude or opRevolve.
Never multiply definition.lengthParam by inch in the body because isLength already returns a Length.
featurePattern: FeatureScript 2931; import geometry.fs; define one exported feature; precondition plane and dimensions; build one stable sketch; skSolve; create body with opExtrude/opRevolve and fCylinder when a primitive cylinder is needed.
failureModes: definition.foo is Length is invalid FeatureScript.
Use fCylinder for simple cylindrical solids instead of opCylinder in this project.
validationRules: Exactly one export const feature should exist.
All sketch entities must be solved before downstream operations.
example_prompt: Create a compile-safe parametric mounting block

title: Parametric Box Body
summary: Use a centered rectangle sketch and blind extrude for robot bodies, housings, and simple block geometry.
parameterHints: Expose width, height, and depth as editable length parameters.
Use a fillet radius parameter only if a rounded edge is explicitly requested.
modelingNotes: Sketch the base profile on a selectable plane with newSketchOnPlane.
Keep the rectangle centered around the origin so later mirrors and mating are easier.
featurePattern: Centered rectangle from -width/2,-height/2 to width/2,height/2, solve sketch, extrude blind to depth.
failureModes: Do not create an off-origin corner rectangle unless the user asks for a datum-corner model.
Do not hardcode dimensions if they can be exposed as parameters.
validationRules: Width, height, and depth must all be greater than zero.
Fillet radius should be less than half the smallest nearby edge.
example_prompt: Robot body 12 inches wide, 6 inches tall, 4 inches deep with 0.25 inch fillets

title: Bushing Or Sleeve
summary: Model bushings and spacers as concentric circles extruded to length.
parameterHints: Expose outer radius, inner radius, and length.
Validate that inner radius stays smaller than outer radius.
modelingNotes: Use one sketch with two concentric circles and extrude the ring region.
Prefer editable radii over hardcoded diameters in the body.
featurePattern: Create two concentric circles in the same sketch, solve, then extrude the annular sketch region.
failureModes: Do not allow the inner radius to equal or exceed the outer radius.
Do not convert a diameter into a radius twice.
validationRules: OD X means outer radius X/2.
ID Y means inner radius Y/2.
example_prompt: Bushing with 0.75 inch outer diameter, 0.5 inch inner diameter, and 1 inch length

title: Linkage Arm
summary: Use a centered bar sketch with end holes for train linkages, couplers, and lever arms.
parameterHints: Expose total length, bar width, thickness, and pin hole radius.
Compute hole offset from total length and hole size to preserve end material.
modelingNotes: Create the outer rectangle and end holes in the same sketch.
Keep holes symmetric unless the prompt explicitly requests asymmetry.
featurePattern: Sketch a centered rounded or rectangular bar, place two symmetric pin holes along the length axis, solve, extrude to thickness.
failureModes: Do not place holes too close to the edge; leave at least 2x hole radius of material.
Do not confuse total length with center-to-center hole spacing.
validationRules: Hole radius must be smaller than half the bar width.
Thickness should be a separate editable depth parameter.
example_prompt: Linkage arm 5 inches long, 1 inch wide, 0.25 inch thick with 0.2 inch pin holes

title: Flange With Bolt Circle
summary: Model circular flanges with a bore and evenly patterned bolt holes.
parameterHints: Expose outer radius, bore radius, hole radius, hole count, and thickness.
If bolt circle diameter is not given, use a derived radius around 70 to 80 percent of outer radius.
modelingNotes: Generate all circles in one sketch before extruding.
Evenly distribute bolt holes using cosine and sine from the center.
featurePattern: Outer circle plus bore circle plus N bolt-hole circles on a bolt circle radius, then extrude the remaining region.
failureModes: Do not put bolt holes outside the flange OD.
Do not make the bore larger than the outer radius.
validationRules: Bolt circle radius plus hole radius must be less than outer radius.
Use at least 3 bolt holes unless the prompt says otherwise.
example_prompt: Round flange 4 inch OD with 1 inch bore and 4 bolt holes

title: L Bracket
summary: Use a simple 2D L profile extruded to length for angle brackets and corner supports.
parameterHints: Expose arm width, arm height, wall thickness, and extrusion length.
Keep wall thickness smaller than both arm dimensions.
modelingNotes: Sketch a closed L profile instead of extruding a full plate and cutting it afterward.
Use simple straight segments for reliability.
featurePattern: Closed L polygon with outside arm dimensions and inside notch based on wall thickness, then extrude along depth.
failureModes: Do not make wall thickness greater than either leg.
Do not leave the L profile open.
validationRules: The polygon must be closed before sketch solve.
Wall thickness should be exposed as an editable parameter.
example_prompt: L bracket 3 inches by 4 inches, 0.25 inch wall, 2 inch long

title: Hitch Peg Or Mushroom Pin
summary: Model a pin with a cylindrical shaft and domed or revolved head.
parameterHints: Expose shaft radius, shaft height, and head radius.
If head height is not provided, approximate a rounded cap from the head radius.
modelingNotes: Create the shaft with a cylinder-like operation and the head with a revolve profile.
Union the head and shaft at the end.
featurePattern: fCylinder shaft from base to height, revolve a half-dome or cap profile around the center axis, then boolean union.
failureModes: Use fCylinder for the shaft primitive and keep the dome as a separate revolved body.
Do not leave the head and shaft as separate bodies unless requested.
validationRules: Head radius should be greater than or equal to shaft radius.
The revolve axis must align with the shaft axis.
example_prompt: Hitch peg with 0.25 inch shaft diameter, 0.5 inch shaft height, and 0.42 inch dome head

title: Spur Gear
summary: Use an involute-inspired 2D tooth profile and extrude it to face width for train gears and pinions.
parameterHints: Expose tooth count and face width; derive pitch geometry from pitch radius or diametral pitch.
Add a bore radius parameter when the gear must mount to a shaft.
modelingNotes: Keep pressure angle at 20 degrees unless the prompt requests otherwise.
Prefer a valid simplified gear profile over an overcomplicated but brittle one.
featurePattern: Generate alternating root/flank/tip/flank points around the pitch circle, solve one closed sketch, then extrude to face width.
failureModes: Do not ask the LLM to invent a full involute API.
Do not generate hundreds of separate sketch operations when a compact loop can create the tooth outline.
validationRules: Tooth count should be at least 6.
Pitch radius, root radius, and tip radius must stay positive and ordered root < pitch < tip.
example_prompt: 20 tooth spur gear with 2 inch pitch diameter and 0.5 inch face width

title: Spur Gear Parameterization
summary: Expose gear pitch radius, tooth count, face width, bore radius, and pressure angle so the generated feature stays editable.
parameterHints: Expose number of teeth as an integer parameter.
Expose pitch radius as a length parameter and compute tooth geometry from it.
Expose pressure angle so the user can adjust tooth form for 14.5°, 20°, or 25° profiles.
modelingNotes: Compute the involute profile using runtime math from the feature definition.
Avoid baking fixed tooth geometry into the generated FeatureScript code.
Use a default face width equal to roughly half the pitch diameter.
featurePattern: Parameterize numTeeth, radius, pressureAngleDegrees, faceWidth, and holeRadius; build each tooth profile in a loop and extrude the resulting sketch.
failureModes: Do not hardcode the number of teeth or pitch radius into the feature body.
Do not omit a user-editable pressure angle when the gear is described as a standard gear.
Do not expose only face width without allowing the user to change the gear size.
validationRules: numTeeth must be an integer and at least 6.
pressureAngleDegrees should be between 10 and 30.
Bore radius must be smaller than pitch radius.
example_prompt: Generate a 24 tooth spur gear with 2.5 inch pitch radius, 20° pressure angle, 0.5 inch face width, and 0.25 inch bore radius

title: Slotted Mounting Plate
summary: For adjustable mounts, use a plate profile with one or more slots instead of only round holes.
parameterHints: Expose plate width, plate height, thickness, slot length, slot width, and slot spacing.
If the prompt is ambiguous, use centered slots with enough margin to the outer edge.
modelingNotes: Build each slot from two circles connected by tangent lines in the same sketch.
Extrude the resulting sketch region with the slot cutouts already present.
featurePattern: Outer rectangle plus each slot as a capsule profile using two equal-radius circles and tangent line segments.
failureModes: Do not make slot width larger than slot length.
Do not place slots beyond plate boundaries.
validationRules: Slot radius is slot width / 2.
Slot center spacing must leave edge margin.
example_prompt: Mounting plate 6 by 3 inches with two 1.5 inch slots

title: Ribbed Bracket Or Gusset
summary: Add triangular ribs or gussets to brackets when stiffness or load support is requested.
parameterHints: Expose rib thickness, rib height, and rib count when the prompt requests reinforcement.
Default rib thickness can be close to wall thickness.
modelingNotes: Keep ribs simple and symmetric for first-pass generated CAD.
A triangular prism rib is usually more robust than complex curved webbing.
featurePattern: Create the base bracket first, then add triangular rib profiles on the side plane and extrude/union them into the bracket.
failureModes: Do not create ribs that float without touching both supported faces.
Do not overcomplicate with lofts unless the user specifically asks.
validationRules: Ribs should intersect the main bracket body.
Rib thickness should be less than the bracket width.
example_prompt: Reinforced L bracket with two triangular gussets

title: Shell Or Enclosure
summary: For cases and housings, model an outer block with editable wall thickness and an open side.
parameterHints: Expose width, height, depth, wall thickness, and optional lid clearance.
Keep wall thickness below one third of the smallest outer dimension.
modelingNotes: Use simple rectangular shell logic before adding bosses, clips, or vents.
If the exact open face is unclear, default to an open top.
featurePattern: Create outer box, create inner offset cavity based on wall thickness, subtract or sketch the ring profile and extrude as a shell-like body.
failureModes: Do not let wall thickness consume the interior cavity.
Do not add tiny snap details unless dimensions are provided.
validationRules: Inner width/height/depth must remain positive.
Open face should match the prompt or default to top.
example_prompt: Small electronics enclosure 4 x 3 x 1.5 inches with 0.1 inch walls

title: Image Based CAD Interpretation
summary: When generating from images, prioritize explicit dimensions and simple manufacturable geometry over visual decoration.
parameterHints: If a dimension is visible, use it directly.
If a dimension is missing, infer conservatively and expose it as an editable parameter.
modelingNotes: Separate what is visible from what is inferred in the reasoning trace.
Use image labels to decide which view controls dimensions.
featurePattern: Vision description -> compact dimension prompt -> extractDims -> AI-authored FeatureScript first -> static validation and repair -> fallback only if fatal issues remain.
failureModes: Do not pass long image descriptions into multiple LLM calls.
Do not treat shadows, perspective, or material texture as required geometry.
validationRules: Generated dimensions should be editable.
If confidence is low, the reasoning should say which dimensions were inferred.
example_prompt: Use this dimensioned drawing to generate the mounting bracket

title: Spur Gear Involute Tooth Math
summary: For spur gears, derive all geometry from pitch radius and tooth count. Pressure angle 20deg is standard. Tip radius = pitch + module. Root radius = pitch - 1.35*module. Base circle = pitch * cos(20deg). Generate tooth profile as an involute curve parametrized by t.
parameterHints: numTeeth: integer, minimum 6. For gear ratios, driven gear teeth = ratio * driver teeth.
radiusInches: pitch radius = numTeeth / (2 * diametralPitch). For 20DP 32T gear: 32/(2*20)=0.8in.
depthInches: face width = 0.4 to 0.8 * pitch diameter. Default 0.5 * pitchDiameter.
holeRadiusInches: bore hole for shaft, typically 0.25 * pitch radius. Set 0 for solid gear.
modelingNotes: AI-authored gear code should compute only the geometry it actually uses and remove dead helper variables before returning the file.
GEAR_SPUR prompts should stay parameter-driven so tooth count, pitch radius, face width, bore, and pressure angle all remain editable.
8:1 gear ratio means one gear has 8x as many teeth as the other. For an 8:1 set at 20DP: pinion=8 teeth (r=0.2in), driven=64 teeth (r=1.6in).
Module (metric) = 25.4 / diametral_pitch. 1mm module = ~25.4 DP. Convert module to inches: pitchRadius = (numTeeth * module_mm) / (2 * 25.4).
featurePattern: extractDims classifies as GEAR_SPUR → AI-authored gear logic computes rb, rd, ra from numTeeth+radiusInches → generates tooth outlines as skFitSpline+skArc calls → skSolve → opExtrude to depthInches.
failureModes: Do not leave unused helper variables such as derived radii or angles in the final gear code.
Do NOT use fCylinder for gears — the tooth profile requires a sketch-based approach.
A gear with fewer than 6 teeth will have undercut problems; enforce minimum 6.
validationRules: tipRadius > pitchRadius > rootRadius > 0 always.
Face width (depthInches) should be 0.2 to 1.5 * pitch diameter.
Bore hole radius must be less than root radius * 0.85.
example_prompt: spur gear 32 teeth 20 diametral pitch 0.5 inch face width with 0.25 inch bore

title: FRC Robot Gear Train Sizing
summary: FRC robots commonly use 20DP or 32DP spur gears for drivetrains. Ratio is driven/driver teeth. Small pinions (8-12T) mesh with large gears (40-64T) for speed reduction. Belt + pulley and chain + sprocket are alternatives but this app generates spur gears.
parameterHints: For 8:1 ratio at 20DP: pinion=8T r=0.2in, driven=64T r=1.6in.
For 4:1 ratio at 20DP: pinion=12T r=0.3in, driven=48T r=1.2in.
Standard FRC gear pitches: 20DP (strong, drivetrain), 32DP (lighter, mechanisms).
Center distance between two meshing gears = pitchRadius1 + pitchRadius2.
modelingNotes: When user says 'gear ratio X:1', generate the driven (larger) gear — it's the useful output shaft gear.
When user says 'pinion', generate the smaller driver gear.
Face width for FRC drivetrain gears is typically 0.375 to 0.75 inches.
featurePattern: Parse ratio → compute numTeeth = ratio * pinion_teeth (default pinion=8) → compute pitchRadius = numTeeth / (2 * diametralPitch) → route to AI-authored GEAR_SPUR logic.
failureModes: Do not confuse gear ratio with number of teeth — ratio 8:1 means 8x as many teeth, not 8 teeth.
Do not make bore holes larger than the root circle.
validationRules: Always produce at least numTeeth=6.
Diametral pitch defaults to 20 for FRC unless stated otherwise.
example_prompt: 8:1 ratio spur gear for FRC drivetrain at 20 diametral pitch

title: Stepped Shaft Or Shoulder Shaft
summary: A shaft with multiple diameters — a smaller section for bearing/bushing seating and a larger section for torque transfer. Build as two coaxial cylinders unioned together.
parameterHints: Expose mainRadius, stepRadius (smaller), mainLength, stepLength.
stepRadius < mainRadius always.
For hex shafts, use a hexagonal polygon cross-section instead of circle.
modelingNotes: Use two fCylinder calls — one for main body, one for stepped end — then opBoolean union.
Stepped shafts in FRC are commonly 0.5 inch hex or round with snap ring grooves.
If user says 'hex shaft', use POLYGON shape with sides=6 instead of CYLINDER.
featurePattern: fCylinder main body → fCylinder step end (smaller radius, positioned at top of main) → opBoolean UNION.
failureModes: Do not teach opCylinder for simple cylindrical solids in this codebase; prefer fCylinder.
Do not forget to union the two bodies.
validationRules: stepRadius must be less than mainRadius.
Both lengths must be positive.
example_prompt: stepped shaft 0.5 inch diameter main section 3 inches long, 0.375 inch step 1 inch long

title: U-Channel Or C-Channel Profile
summary: Structural channel used in FRC robots. A U or C cross-section extruded to length. Sketch the open profile as a closed U polygon, then extrude.
parameterHints: Expose channelWidth, channelHeight, wallThickness, and length.
Keep wall thickness 0.05 to 0.25 inches for aluminum extrusions.
MaxTube (FRC common): 2x1x0.1 or 1x1x0.1 inch cross-section.
modelingNotes: Sketch the U profile as 6 line segments forming the open channel cross-section, solve, then extrude along length.
Avoid opShell — sketch the profile directly for reliability.
For box tube (closed), use two concentric rectangles and extrude the ring region.
featurePattern: Sketch closed U polygon (outer W x H, subtract inner cavity based on wall thickness), skSolve, opExtrude to length.
failureModes: Open sketch profiles will fail skSolve — ensure the U is closed at the bottom.
Do not use opShell — it requires a solid body first and often fails on thin walls.
validationRules: Wall thickness must be less than half of both width and height.
Inner cavity must remain positive (width - 2*wall > 0).
example_prompt: 2x1 inch aluminum U-channel 12 inches long 0.1 inch wall thickness

title: Pulley Or Belt Wheel
summary: Timing belt pulleys have a specific tooth profile. For FeatureScript generation, approximate as a cylinder with the pitch diameter as the main dimension and expose tooth count and belt pitch.
parameterHints: GT2 belt: pitch = 2mm = 0.0787 inch. pitchDiameter = numTeeth * 2mm / pi.
HTD 5mm belt: pitch = 5mm = 0.1969 inch.
Expose numTeeth, beltPitch, faceWidth, flangeDiameter, boreRadius.
modelingNotes: A simplified pulley is a cylinder with pitch diameter. For FeatureScript, use CYLINDER or BUSHING shape.
Use tCylinder or tBushing template with radius = pitchDiameter/2.
Tooth profile detail is typically not needed for FRC part studios — use simplified cylinder.
featurePattern: For GT2 20T pulley: pitchDiameter = 20 * 2mm / pi = 12.73mm = 0.501in → tCylinder with radiusInches=0.25.
failureModes: Do not confuse pitch diameter with outer diameter — pulley OD is slightly larger than pitch diameter.
Do not try to generate individual belt teeth in FeatureScript — too complex and not needed for most uses.
validationRules: Pitch diameter = numTeeth * beltPitch / pi.
Bore must be less than pitch radius.
example_prompt: GT2 20 tooth timing pulley 5mm wide with 8mm bore

title: Bearing Block Or Pillow Block
summary: A block with a circular bore for press-fitting a bearing. Typically a rectangular block with a centered circular cutout sized to the bearing OD.
parameterHints: Common FRC bearings: 0.5in bore (OD 1.125in), 0.375in bore (OD 0.875in), R8 (0.5in bore OD 1.125in).
Press fit bore: bearing OD + 0 to -0.001in interference.
Expose blockWidth, blockHeight, blockDepth, boreRadius.
modelingNotes: Use PLATE_HOLES with numHoles=1 and holeRadius=bearingOD/2, or BOX with centered bore.
Add mounting holes using FLANGE or PLATE_HOLES pattern around the bore.
Keep block thickness equal to or slightly less than bearing width.
featurePattern: Rectangle plate sketch + centered circle for bore, skSolve with true (subtract), opExtrude BLIND to blockDepth.
failureModes: Bore diameter must match the bearing OD precisely — wrong size means the bearing won't seat.
Block depth should not be less than bearing width.
validationRules: boreRadius = bearingOD / 2.
Block must be wide enough to leave wall material around the bore (blockWidth > boreRadius * 2.5).
example_prompt: bearing block for 1.125 inch OD bearing 1.5 inches square and 0.75 inches thick
